messages:
sara: heads up — saw a cluster of small Xid spikes across two racks in us-west-2 over the last hour. pattern looks like short correlated bursts, not a single persistent card failure. filing here before we tune rules.

matt: can you paste the node ids / sample logs? wondering if this is cross-pod network/driver churn or real ECC flake.

sara: node ids: gpu-node-uw2-11, gpu-node-uw2-17. logs show `Xid 31` bursts, each 30–90s, repeated ~6x in last 40m. DCGM exporter increments align with container restarts on a few worker pods.

lee: thanks — my immediate thought: our static threshold rules are tripping too easily when baseline shifts. we should try a rolling-baseline detection instead of absolute counts.

sara: agreed. proposal: create a Prom rule that compares short-window increase to a rolling 7d baseline percentile (95th). only alert if short-window > 3x baseline and the bursts are correlated across >=2 GPUs in the same rack within 10m. reduces noise from single-card flakiness.

matt: sounds good. can you sketch the proto rule? also we need a quick triage playbook for when this fires.

sara: proto rule snippet: ```yaml
- alert: DCGM_GPU_ECC_Drift
  expr: (increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[5m]) > 0)
    and (increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[5m]) > 3 * avg_over_time(increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[5m])[7d:5m]))
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: warning
    team: infra
  annotations:
    summary: "ECC/Xid burst > 3x vs 7d rolling baseline"
    runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-ecc-drift"```

lee: minor tweak — use `quantile_over_time(0.95, ...)` for baseline instead of avg to be resilient to past spikes. and add a `count by (rack) (dcgm_xid_errors_total > 0)` correlation check: only escalate if count >=2.

matt: +1. also recommend adding a suppression window for nodes already tagged `replace_pending` to avoid noisy alerts during replacement.

infra-bot: deploy-check passed for prometheus rule doc change at 1755554400. staging rule applied to canary cluster.

sara: operational playbook draft (short):
1) When alert fires: inspect `dcgm_ecc_errors_total` and `dcgm_xid_errors_total` for nodes referenced; check `kubectl get pods --field-selector` for same timestamps.
2) If multiple GPUs in same rack affected -> roll immediate probe job to collect `dmesg`/driver logs and nvml diagnostics (use `scripts/gpu-quick-probe.sh`).
3) If single GPU affected repeatedly -> mark node `drain:soft`, schedule node lab triage (possible NVLink/seat issue).
4) If patterns repeat across replacement history -> tag `fleet:investigate` and open infra ticket.

matt: can we add a metric for short-term correlation score? something like `sum by (rack) (increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[5m]) > 0)` > 1 -> set label.

lee: yep — will add a derived metric `gpu_xid_correlated_burst` computed in PromQL and use it in the alert. also add `for: 15m` on escalation alert to avoid noisy flaps.

opsbot: reminder: schedule weekly review of nodes with >3 drift alerts in 14d window. auto-annotate tickets for nodes hitting that threshold.

sara: deploy plan: 1) land canary rule in staging (done by infra-bot), 2) run for 48h, capture hit-rate and false positives, 3) extend to us-west-2 only for 7 days, 4) roll global with runbook / playbook updated.

matt: sounds safe. Sara can you post a sample alert payload (labels/annotations) so paging rules can be tuned?

sara: posted sample to the runbook link and added a quick `kubectl` troubleshooting checklist in the runbook. will monitor canary and report back in this thread in ~24h. :thumbsup:

lee: thanks — if canary looks clean we should also add an automated `node:soft-drain` job that runs a non-disruptive probe before marking nodes for replacement. reduces churn.

infra-bot: canary metrics exported: `gpu_xid_correlated_burst` fired 2 times in staging in the last 3h, both suppressed by `replace_pending` label. no page sent. (ts 1755554460)

sara: perfect. I'll watch and close the loop.
